task: Safety and unintended-consequence analysis of proposed outcome-dependent optimisations
supersedes: Risk assessment and implementation priority in report.json; original measurements remain valid

conclusion.reject: Skipping all race validation based solely on race PB or weekly rank
recommended_first: RCO07: conservative early return from newspaper candidate reads
RCO04: negotiated smaller pending responses with equivalent current authorization
RCO05: additive terminal enrichment with exact receipts and monotonic account revisions
conditional_followups: RCO03: standings reuse with participant-eligibility consistency
RCO02: deferred ghosts only after durable references, recovery and reader support
conclusion.defer: RCO06: series aggregate no-op elimination has less SQL benefit than initially implied and changes an observable source reference

corrections_to_first_review: The unchanged series total is already omitted from SQL UPDATE. The observed write changes member.run_id only. Eliminating it is a semantic/reference-retention change, not a simple identical-value write optimisation.
A Rivalry group row lock does not by itself freeze Player.disabled, which standings_data filters. Own weekly time unchanged is insufficient to prove that two live standings reads are identical.
Challenge snapshot construction performs viewer-specific block checks. Keeping available() while removing snapshot() does not preserve the complete current visibility boundary.
Current Rivalry/Challenge ghost readers return 404 when the selected run lacks ghost_hash; deferring winning-source storage needs a compatible recovery/serving path.

findings.verdict: unsafe as a blanket verification bypass
findings.consequence: An unvalidated completion could receive earned effects, or a valid slower race could lose lap-PB rewards, weekly first completion, achievements or exact challenge-source eligibility.
concrete_evidence: A fixture race slower than the lifetime PB still improved the first weekly result and earned 30 weekly points.
A 120-tick attempt left the 100-tick race PB unchanged but established a 10-tick flying-lap PB and received the New lap PB reward.
conditions: Retain the existing lightweight path, pinned-build, ticket, rewind-receipt and account validation.
Only skip downstream competitive work whose actual server-owned inputs are unchanged.
Use strict integer race/flying-lap/weekly/stage comparisons within the same track version, car and rules board. Preserve ties, first completions and exact slower source runs.
Do not rely on submitted noncompetitive flags or local cached times to authorize rewards.

findings.verdict: safe only as a coordinated deferred-presentation design
consequences: A newly retained weekly/stage source can be slower than the lifetime PB; checking lifetime PB alone would lose its recording.
Publishing a source before its separate ghost is recoverable makes existing recording endpoints return 404.
Deferring upload to the client can lose recordings after shutdown, device/account change or local cleanup.
Retention, object collection, account erasure and concurrent winners can race with a later materialization job.
Cold object reads and ghost reconstruction can move latency/failure into challenge creation or Race Again.
findings.concrete_evidence: A current Challenge recording endpoint returned 200 with the stored ghost_hash and 404 after clearing that hash in the disposable fixture.
conditions: Retain the exact submitted evidence and necessary ghost bytes durably until all future source uses in the supported retention window are covered.
Check all retained references: race/lap PBs where needed, weekly slots, challenge targets/member/stage sources and creator evidence.
Support on-demand serving or materialization before publishing a source that existing readers expect to be immediately readable.
Use idempotent jobs, original hash/build identity, object pins and post-I/O account/source revalidation. Never resurrect erased content.
Keep disk/object I/O outside competition locks.
Measure net savings: omitting the standalone object copy does not eliminate embedded ghost upload/storage bytes.

findings.verdict: conditionally safe within a defined, consistent participant snapshot
consequences: A suspension or other participant eligibility change can alter ranks/points while the current run fails to improve its weekly time.
Reusing pre-improvement data for comeback achievements changes the pre/post distinction.
Sharing mutable standings across requests/viewers risks stale or viewer-inappropriate decoration.
findings.concrete_evidence: An injected participant suspension between two reads changed the slower attempt's position from 2 to 1 and points_delta to 4 with improved=false.
conditions: Keep reuse transaction-local and preserve separate before and after snapshots when a best changes.
Provide a coherent eligibility snapshot or a fenced eligibility revision/recheck with fallback; the group lock alone is insufficient.
Preserve exact outcome, week boundaries, ties and achievement post-result inputs.
Do not introduce broad participant locks without measuring contention and deadlock behavior.
findings.evidence_limit: The eligibility change was injected in one SQLite fixture transaction; it demonstrates data dependence, not a real PostgreSQL concurrency result.

findings.verdict: safe with equivalent authorization and negotiated client support
consequences: Moving directly from available() to a small response would omit current viewer/creator block checks embedded in snapshot().
The existing client requires a valid challenge snapshot on every result read and would treat a slim response as an error.
The displayed attempts, opponent standings, cancellation, expiry and UTC-day reward availability can become stale while a run stays queued.
findings.concrete_evidence: A pending result read returned 200, then 403 after the challenger blocked the challenge creator. The viewer-specific enforcement resides in snapshot construction.
conditions: Extract and preserve the existing current authorization/visibility checks before choosing a compact representation.
Advertise a capability; continue full responses for existing clients.
Preserve ticket/account/session fences, retry timing, unavailable/expired/cancelled handling and fresh terminal data.
Define refresh behavior for elapsed time, day boundaries and external competition changes rather than assuming no row change means no visible change.
Return complete requested terminal information and retain an explicit full-refresh fallback.

findings.verdict: safe as additive, bounded terminal-response enrichment
consequences: A delayed completion response can overwrite a newer wallet after another race or purchase.
Adding a receipt amount locally on each reply can count duplicated responses twice.
A slow/missing old archive or failed optional enrichment can make the entire combined endpoint unavailable if failures are coupled.
Joining extra account data for every pending read or duplicating it for every item in a 32-run batch may increase database work and payloads.
Achievement rarity and background creator/competition awards can change independently of this race's account-state revision.
conditions: Send only committed receipt/outcome data, tied to the original ticket/run.
Apply absolute wallet snapshots monotonically by server revision and retain account/origin/session generation fences; do not mint via local addition.
Include terminal enrichment only as needed and share account state once per batch.
Keep result status recoverable when optional receipt/archive enrichment is temporarily unavailable; retain existing fallback endpoints and durable outbox identities.
Use revision domains that actually cover each rendered component and preserve background achievement refresh paths.
Never call an award writer as a side effect of a read.

consequences: A slower attempt changes the public top-level member.run_id despite an unchanged aggregate time.
That reference is also part of ordinary retention protection; skipping its change alters which exact run remains protected.
Most stage reads remain necessary to build completed-track counts and result feedback; summing at most five integers is small work.

concrete_evidence.current_sql: UPDATE challenge_members SET run_id=? WHERE challenge_members.challenge_id = ? AND challenge_members.player_id = ?

conditions: Clarify and test representative-run semantics before eliminating the reference write.
Preserve stage bests, first completion, limited starts, exact per-attempt result and coin/achievement effects.
Measure a meaningful query/write reduction instead of counting an unchanged ORM assignment as a SQL write.
findings.excluded_claim: No current series-rematch regression is claimed; that endpoint explicitly rejects series rematches.

findings.verdict: lowest-risk candidate: conservative early skip only
consequences: A race-only gate loses a flying-lap world-record/reach path on a slower overall race.
A missing previous PB must count as a first improvement.
Pre-lock/client-derived or rounded improvement guesses can disagree with the committed PB projections.
conditions: Calculate both strict race and eligible flying-lap improvement possibilities from existing locked server acceptance facts.
Ignore the standing first lap exactly as the lap projection does; use integer ticks.
Return early only when neither can improve. Keep the current actual-source candidate query and all eligibility/record/reach logic for every possible improvement.
Retain same-transaction finalization and original once-only result fences; do not use the flags themselves to announce a winning source.
findings.evidence: Source dependency review plus the slower-race/new-lap-PB counterexample; no new early-return implementation or equivalence claim.

validation.regression_command: .tools/backend-venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest backend/tests/test_challenges.py backend/tests/test_challenge_series.py backend/tests/test_race_acceptance_sql.py backend/tests/test_news.py -k 'not postgres and (finished_ticket_pins_slower or pending_finished_ticket or independent_budgets or every_stage_obeys or late_ledger_failure or new_revisions_and_rolled_back or mutual_friend_requests)' -q -rs --disable-warnings
validation.limitation: Checks validate current contracts and demonstrate hazards. They do not certify proposed, unimplemented changes or production-shaped PostgreSQL concurrency.

remaining_acceptance: Implement only within the stated constraints; compare rewards, balances, exact source references, standings, current authorization and retry outcomes before and after.
Exercise simultaneous same-player and competing-player finalization, account/content removal, lost replies, ghost materialization failure and cleanup in disposable PostgreSQL.
For protocol changes, test old and new clients, out-of-order replies, account switches, offline recovery and midnight/week rollover.
Measure actual endpoint SQL/WAL/object/byte savings and result-screen latency before rollout.
